*REMINDER: Online registration for Winter Fun Program remains open*

LĪHU‘E –The Department of Parks and Recreation announces that online registration for the County’s Winter Fun Program remains open, with spaces still available.

Interested participants may register by visiting the Department of Parks and Recreation’s Winter Fun page and clicking on “Online Registration”.

The Winter Fun Program is open to children ages 5 to 11 and runs from December 21 through December 31, Monday through Thursday, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The program will be closed on December 25 and January 1 in observance of the holidays.

Program sites include the Kekaha, Kalāheo, Kapaa, and Līhu‘e neighborhood centers. The cost of enrollment is $50 per child, and does not include lunch.

Enrollment is limited and will be handled on a first-come, first-served basis.

Parents or guardians will need to provide lunch, beverages, and snacks for their child or children on a daily basis.

For more information about the Winter Fun Program, please visit www.kauai.gov/parks or call (808) 241-4465 or (808) 241-4467.

If you need an auxiliary aid/service or other accommodation due to a disability, contact James Kealalio at (808) 241-4467 or jkealalio@kauai.gov as soon as possible. Requests made as early as possible will allow adequate time to fulfill your request. Upon request, this notice is available in alternate formats such as large print, Braille, or electronic copy.

Mayor Kawakami signs Bill 2998, bringing wildfire safety standards to new homes islandwide

LĪHUʻE – On Monday, Nov. 16, Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami signed into law Bill No. 2998, Draft 3, an ordinance passed by the Kauaʻi County Council on Oct. 28 that sets islandwide wildfire safety standards for new homes.

The ordinance establishes Wildfire and Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) construction requirements for new homes and substantial improvements, along with defensible space, setback, and access standards for larger new developments. It builds on Bill No. 2961, signed in September 2025, which made Kauaʻi the first county in Hawaiʻi to tie wildfire safety into zoning and permitting for West Kauaʻi’s plantation camp districts.

“Mahalo to the Kauaʻi County Council, our Planning Department, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency, the Hawaiʻi Wildfire Management Organization, and the builders, designers, and residents who testified and helped shape this ordinance,” said Mayor Kawakami. “Lahaina taught all of Hawaiʻi that in a wind-driven fire, homes are lost to embers. We have a kuleana to learn from that before we face a disaster of our own. The homes we build today will be home to our keiki and kūpuna for generations, and this ordinance makes sure they are built with that lesson in mind.”

According to U.S. Department of Agriculture Forest Service data cited in the ordinance, homes in Kauaʻi County face a higher wildfire risk than about 91 percent of U.S. counties. The Lahaina Fire Incident Analysis Report also recommended WUI codes, ember-resistant construction, and defensible space requirements as key steps for wildfire safety statewide.

“As our climate changes, we have to do everything we can on the planning side before a fire ever starts,” said Council Planning Committee Chair Addison Bulosan. “No one takes added building costs lightly, and this Council spent months working through those questions with our community. In the end, protecting lives and homes is worth it.”

GD-PIO NR 11-14-26 (Distressed hikers rescued on Kalalau Trail Friday)
2026-11-15T01:01:36 [other]
*Distressed hikers rescued on Kalalau Trail Friday*

LĪHU‘E  — Personnel from the Kauaʻi Fire Department rescued two female visitors from the Hanakāpīʻai area on Friday, November 13. A 39-year-old female hiker experienced a medical emergency, while the 35-year-old female hiker sustained an ankle injury.

Rescue 3 aboard Air 1 responded to the incident shortly before 4:45 p.m. on Friday after receiving reports of a hiker experiencing chest pain and difficulty breathing, and unable to hike out.

Upon reaching the area, rescuers located both hikers near the Hanakāpīʻai Beach landing zone. The first hiker, who was experiencing a medical emergency and dehydration, was loaded into Air 1 and transported to Princeville Airport, where she was transferred to American Medical Response (AMR) personnel with assistance from Hanalei Fire Station personnel.

Air 1 then returned to the area and transported the second hiker, who had sustained an alleged ankle injury, to Princeville Airport, where she was also transferred to AMR personnel.

The scene was cleared shortly before 6:37 p.m. View as web page

*Nov. 13 UPDATE: *The Kaua’i Police Department (KPD) located juvenile runaway Talula Kuzemka this afternoon. The 17-year-old was found safe. KPD expresses gratitude to the public for their assistance.

*Police seek public’s help locating runaway 17-year-old*

LĪHU‘E – The Kaua’I Police Department (KPD) is requesting the public’s assistance in locating a missing 17-year old.

Talula Kuzemka, 17, of Kapa’a, has been reported missing. She is described as 5 feet 6 inches tall, approximately 116 pounds, with light brown hair, and brown eyes. She was last seen on the evening of Oct. 23 at her residence on Hau’aala Road in Kapa’a.

Anyone with information is encouraged to contact KPD Dispatch at (808) 241-1711. To remain anonymous, contact Crime Stoppers Kaua’i at (808) 246-8300, submit a tip at crimestopperskauai.org , or use the Crime Stoppers Kaua’i P3 Tips Mobile App. View as web page

2026-11-11T20:12:07 [weather]
*Officials advise no swimming, recreational ocean activities on north- and west-facing shores*

HANALEI *– *Ocean Safety Bureau officials are advising no swimming or other recreational ocean activities along all north- and west-facing shores of Kauaʻi today through Thursday, Nov. 12, due to high surf and dangerous ocean conditions.

The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Advisory for north- and west-facing shores of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau, in effect until 6 p.m. Thursday.

According to the NWS, a large north-northwest swell will build through the day, with surf rising to 15 to 20 feet along north-facing shores and 10 to 15 feet along west-facing shores. Surf is expected to peak tonight at 18 to 24 feet on north-facing shores and 14 to 18 feet on west-facing shores, possibly into Thursday morning, before dropping below advisory levels Thursday night.

Forecasters also expect breezy trade winds, with strong, gusty winds possible on Kauaʻi. A Small Craft Advisory is in effect for Kauaʻi waters until 6 a.m. Thursday. Another swell this weekend could bring surf back to advisory levels.

As a safety precaution, OSB officials have posted warning signs and are monitoring the area.

Entering the water in these areas in hazardous ocean conditions could cause serious injury or death. Beachgoers are also advised to use extreme caution, as large breaking waves could make it dangerous for those standing along the shoreline. When in doubt, don’t go out.

Beachgoers are urged to heed all posted warnings and advisories.

For updated information on ocean and weather alerts, visit the NWS website, www.weather.gov/hfo.

For up-to-date information about Kauaʻi ocean conditions and ocean safety, please speak to a county lifeguard at any lifeguard station, visit safebeachday.com/county/kauai, or call the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984. View as web page

*Temporary green waste sites in Kapaʻa and Kīlauea to close Nov. 17*

LĪHUʻE – The County of Kauaʻi Department of Public Works Solid Waste Division will close its temporary green waste sites in Kapaʻa and Kīlauea on Tuesday, Nov. 17.

The two sites opened after Hurricane Lowell as a short-term option to help residents clear storm-related green waste. Closing them on schedule keeps the County’s storm debris operations within federal disaster recovery requirements.

“These sites were set up to help our ʻohana clean up after the storm, and they were always meant to be temporary,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “Closing them now is the responsible step to protect the recovery funding our island depends on. Mahalo to our Solid Waste team for keeping these sites running, and to everyone who came out with patience and aloha.”

After Nov. 17, residents may continue to recycle green waste at the following County facilities, open daily except holidays:


* Hanalei Refuse Transfer Station, 5-3751 Kūhiō Highway, Princeville. Green waste is accepted from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m.
* Kapaʻa Refuse Transfer Station, 5051 Kahi Road, Kapaʻa. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m.
* Līhuʻe Refuse Transfer Station, 3450 Ahukini Road, Līhuʻe. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m.
* Hanapēpē Refuse Transfer Station, 4380 Lele Road, Hanapēpē. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m.
* Kekaha Landfill, 6900-D Kaumualiʻi Highway, Kekaha. 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed for lunch from noon to 12:30 p.m.

Green waste is also accepted for a fee at these permitted private facilities. Please call ahead for hours and rates:


* Heart and Soul Organics, 6020 Koʻolau Road, Moloaʻa. 808-823-1007
* Green Earth Matters, next to Heart and Soul Organics, Moloaʻa. 808-651-2058
* Kauai Nursery and Landscaping, 3-1550 Kaumualiʻi Highway, Līhuʻe. 808-245-7747

Green waste includes lawn trimmings, yard waste, tree trimmings, stumps, branches, leaves, and shrubbery. Only green waste is accepted. Remove all rope, tarps, plastic bags, and tie-downs before dropping off. Logs and stumps 8 inches or more in diameter should be cut to 8 feet or less.

Through Nov. 17, there is no fee to drop off Hurricane Lowell debris at County refuse transfer stations or the Kekaha Landfill. The fee waiver, part of the County emergency order signed Sept. 18, applies to homes and businesses and covers hurricane debris only.

2026-11-10T01:39:08 [power, water, roads, debris, shelter, transit, county_services, weather, safety]
*Nov. 9, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

*LĪHUʻE – *Please see the latest updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services below.

*Hurricane Lowell Recovery*

*_Hurricane Lowell CASPER survey next week_*

The Hawaiʻi Department of Health’s Kauaʻi District Health Office and the County of Kauaʻi will conduct a Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response (CASPER) survey Nov. 16 to 20 to learn about Hurricane Lowell impacts and ongoing recovery needs. The results will help guide recovery work by county, state, and federal partners and community organizations.


* Teams will go door to door in 30 randomly selected areas, visiting seven homes in each area.
* Teams are made up of DOH staff, supported by the Kauaʻi Medical Reserve Corps and KEMA. Members will wear identifying vests and carry ID cards.
* The survey takes less than 10 minutes and is voluntary. Responses are confidential, and no names or addresses are collected. Households may also complete the survey by phone.
* Questions cover emergency supplies right after the storm, physical and economic impacts, health and well-being, and recovery needs.
* Results will be shared in a public report. Past Kauaʻi CASPER reports are at https://health.hawaii.gov/kauai/Casper.

*_Relief grants for farmers and ranchers_*

Farmers and ranchers whose agricultural lands were affected by Hurricane Lowell and other recent storms may apply for up to $1,500 through the state’s Emergency Farmer Relief grant program. Applications close Jan. 29, 2027.


* Farms, orchards, ranches, and similar operations statewide are eligible. Limit one $1,500 check per applicant per year.
* Applicants must provide tax documents such as a W-9, Schedule C, or Schedule F.
* Funding is limited. If applications exceed available funds, they will be processed first-come, first-served.
* Checks are expected to be available for pickup statewide starting early to mid-January. Applicants will be notified of the time and place.

* Apply at https://dab.hawaii.gov. For questions, email dab.info@hawaii.gov or call (808) 973-9560.

*_Business Recovery Grants_*

Due to high demand, the Kauaʻi Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program is no longer accepting applications. Businesses and nonprofits can join the waitlist at https://kauaibusinessrecovery.org in case more funding becomes available.

The *EISPN document will be available to download* from the* State of Hawaii - Environmental Review Program website on November 8, 2026:*

Mayor Kawakami signs Bill 2998, bringing wildfire safety standards to new homes islandwide

LĪHUʻE – On Monday, Nov. 16, Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami signed into law Bill No. 2998, Draft 3, an ordinance passed by the Kauaʻi County Council on Oct. 28 that sets islandwide wildfire safety standards for new homes.

The ordinance establishes Wildfire and Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) construction requirements for new homes and substantial improvements, along with defensible space, setback, and access standards for larger new developments. It builds on Bill No. 2961, signed in September 2025, which made Kauaʻi the first county in Hawaiʻi to tie wildfire safety into zoning and permitting for West Kauaʻi’s plantation camp districts.

“Mahalo to the Kauaʻi County Council, our Planning Department, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency, the Hawaiʻi Wildfire Management Organization, and the builders, designers, and residents who testified and helped shape this ordinance,” said Mayor Kawakami. “Lahaina taught all of Hawaiʻi that in a wind-driven fire, homes are lost to embers. We have a kuleana to learn from that before we face a disaster of our own. The homes we build today will be home to our keiki and kūpuna for generations, and this ordinance makes sure they are built with that lesson in mind.”

According to U.S. Department of Agriculture Forest Service data cited in the ordinance, homes in Kauaʻi County face a higher wildfire risk than about 91 percent of U.S. counties. The Lahaina Fire Incident Analysis Report also recommended WUI codes, ember-resistant construction, and defensible space requirements as key steps for wildfire safety statewide.

“As our climate changes, we have to do everything we can on the planning side before a fire ever starts,” said Council Planning Committee Chair Addison Bulosan. “No one takes added building costs lightly, and this Council spent months working through those questions with our community. In the end, protecting lives and homes is worth it.”

Under the ordinance, new homes will include home hardening standards, a non-combustible zone, and setback standards for future subdivisions.

“This ordinance was built for Kauaʻi, not copied from a mainland code,” said Planning Director Kaʻāina Hull. “Every requirement was weighed for its safety benefit, its cost, and whether it lets us keep building the housing our community needs. The focus is on embers and the fuels around a home, which is where homes are saved or lost.”

The cost of construction under the code will also be offset by a Kauai Water Department facilities reserve charge (FRC) waiver of $14,000 for the implementation of wildfire regulations, making many proposed homes actually cheaper to construct under the WUI bill than under current code standards.

“Most homes lost in wildfires are ignited by embers, often well ahead of the fire itself,” said Kauaʻi Fire Department Chief Michael Gibson. “A clear 5-foot zone, covered metal gutters, ember-resistant vents, and well-kept defensible space give a home a fighting chance during Red Flag Warning conditions, and they give our firefighters a safer place to work.”

The bill also addresses the rising cost of homeowners insurance. Increasing risks associated with climate-related hazards, including wildfires, are contributing to reduced insurance availability, and increasing premiums are affecting the overall affordability of home ownership. This bill aligns with wildfire mitigation standards of the Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety (IBHS) to strengthen property resilience and help improve insurance affordability on Kauaʻi.

The Planning Department developed the ordinance over two years with the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency, the Building Division, the Hawaiʻi Wildfire Management Organization (HWMO), DoKi Wildfire Solutions, and UL Research Institutes’ Fire Safety Research Institute (FSRI). paragraphs: LĪHU‘E  — Personnel from the Kauaʻi Fire Department rescued two female visitors from the Hanakāpīʻai area on Friday, November 13. A 39-year-old female hiker experienced a medical emergency, while the 35-year-old female hiker sustained an ankle injury.
Rescue 3 aboard Air 1 responded to the incident shortly before 4:45 p.m. on Friday after receiving reports of a hiker experiencing chest pain and difficulty breathing, and unable to hike out.

Upon reaching the area, rescuers located both hikers near the Hanakāpīʻai Beach landing zone. The first hiker, who was experiencing a medical emergency and dehydration, was loaded into Air 1 and transported to Princeville Airport, where she was transferred to American Medical Response (AMR) personnel with assistance from Hanalei Fire Station personnel.
Air 1 then returned to the area and transported the second hiker, who had sustained an alleged ankle injury, to Princeville Airport, where she was also transferred to AMR personnel.
The scene was cleared shortly before 6:37 p.m.

LĪHU‘E – The Kaua’I Police Department (KPD) is requesting the public’s assistance in locating a missing 17-year old.

Talula Kuzemka, 17, of Kapa’a, has been reported missing. She is described as 5 feet 6 inches tall, approximately 116 pounds, with light brown hair, and brown eyes. She was last seen on the evening of Oct. 23 at her residence on Hau’aala Road in Kapa’a.

Anyone with information is encouraged to contact KPD Dispatch at (808) 241-1711. To remain anonymous, contact Crime Stoppers Kaua’i at (808) 246-8300, submit a tip at crimestopperskauai.org , or use the Crime Stoppers Kaua’i P3 Tips Mobile App.

headline.subject: NR 11-11-26 (Officials advise no swimming, recreational ocean activities on north- and west-facing shores)

items.body:
*Officials advise no swimming, recreational ocean activities on north- and west-facing shores*

HANALEI *– *Ocean Safety Bureau officials are advising no swimming or other recreational ocean activities along all north- and west-facing shores of Kauaʻi today through Thursday, Nov. 12, due to high surf and dangerous ocean conditions.

The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Advisory for north- and west-facing shores of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau, in effect until 6 p.m. Thursday.

According to the NWS, a large north-northwest swell will build through the day, with surf rising to 15 to 20 feet along north-facing shores and 10 to 15 feet along west-facing shores. Surf is expected to peak tonight at 18 to 24 feet on north-facing shores and 14 to 18 feet on west-facing shores, possibly into Thursday morning, before dropping below advisory levels Thursday night.

Forecasters also expect breezy trade winds, with strong, gusty winds possible on Kauaʻi. A Small Craft Advisory is in effect for Kauaʻi waters until 6 a.m. Thursday. Another swell this weekend could bring surf back to advisory levels.

As a safety precaution, OSB officials have posted warning signs and are monitoring the area.

Entering the water in these areas in hazardous ocean conditions could cause serious injury or death. Beachgoers are also advised to use extreme caution, as large breaking waves could make it dangerous for those standing along the shoreline. When in doubt, don’t go out.

Beachgoers are urged to heed all posted warnings and advisories.

For updated information on ocean and weather alerts, visit the NWS website, www.weather.gov/hfo.

For up-to-date information about Kauaʻi ocean conditions and ocean safety, please speak to a county lifeguard at any lifeguard station, visit safebeachday.com/county/kauai, or call the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984.

headline.subject: NR 11-10-26 (Temporary green waste sites in Kapaʻa and Kīlauea to close Nov. 17)

items.body:
*Temporary green waste sites in Kapaʻa and Kīlauea to close Nov. 17*

LĪHUʻE – The County of Kauaʻi Department of Public Works Solid Waste Division will close its temporary green waste sites in Kapaʻa and Kīlauea on Tuesday, Nov. 17.

The two sites opened after Hurricane Lowell as a short-term option to help residents clear storm-related green waste. Closing them on schedule keeps the County’s storm debris operations within federal disaster recovery requirements.

“These sites were set up to help our ʻohana clean up after the storm, and they were always meant to be temporary,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “Closing them now is the responsible step to protect the recovery funding our island depends on. Mahalo to our Solid Waste team for keeping these sites running, and to everyone who came out with patience and aloha.”

After Nov. 17, residents may continue to recycle green waste at the following County facilities, open daily except holidays:


  * Hanalei Refuse Transfer Station, 5-3751 Kūhiō Highway, Princeville. Green waste is accepted from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. 
  * Kapaʻa Refuse Transfer Station, 5051 Kahi Road, Kapaʻa. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. 
  * Līhuʻe Refuse Transfer Station, 3450 Ahukini Road, Līhuʻe. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. 
  * Hanapēpē Refuse Transfer Station, 4380 Lele Road, Hanapēpē. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. 
  * Kekaha Landfill, 6900-D Kaumualiʻi Highway, Kekaha. 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed for lunch from noon to 12:30 p.m. 

Green waste is also accepted for a fee at these permitted private facilities. Please call ahead for hours and rates:


  * Heart and Soul Organics, 6020 Koʻolau Road, Moloaʻa. 808-823-1007 
  * Green Earth Matters, next to Heart and Soul Organics, Moloaʻa. 808-651-2058 
  * Kauai Nursery and Landscaping, 3-1550 Kaumualiʻi Highway, Līhuʻe. 808-245-7747 

Green waste includes lawn trimmings, yard waste, tree trimmings, stumps, branches, leaves, and shrubbery. Only green waste is accepted. Remove all rope, tarps, plastic bags, and tie-downs before dropping off. Logs and stumps 8 inches or more in diameter should be cut to 8 feet or less.

Through Nov. 17, there is no fee to drop off Hurricane Lowell debris at County refuse transfer stations or the Kekaha Landfill. The fee waiver, part of the County emergency order signed Sept. 18, applies to homes and businesses and covers hurricane debris only.

Vehicles and trailers over 3/4-ton capacity are not allowed at County refuse transfer stations. After the waiver ends, vehicles with commercial plates must buy tipping fee coupons to drop off green waste.

For current transfer station hours and service updates, visit www.kauai.gov/TransferStations .

We appreciate your patience, understanding, and cooperation.

For more information, please contact the Solid Waste Division at 808-241-4841.

*Nov. 9, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

*LĪHUʻE – *Please see the latest updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services below.

*Hurricane Lowell Recovery*

*_Hurricane Lowell CASPER survey next week_*

The Hawaiʻi Department of Health’s Kauaʻi District Health Office and the County of Kauaʻi will conduct a Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response (CASPER) survey Nov. 16 to 20 to learn about Hurricane Lowell impacts and ongoing recovery needs. The results will help guide recovery work by county, state, and federal partners and community organizations.


  * Teams will go door to door in 30 randomly selected areas, visiting seven homes in each area. 
  * Teams are made up of DOH staff, supported by the Kauaʻi Medical Reserve Corps and KEMA. Members will wear identifying vests and carry ID cards. 
  * The survey takes less than 10 minutes and is voluntary. Responses are confidential, and no names or addresses are collected. Households may also complete the survey by phone. 
  * Questions cover emergency supplies right after the storm, physical and economic impacts, health and well-being, and recovery needs. 
  * Results will be shared in a public report. Past Kauaʻi CASPER reports are at https://health.hawaii.gov/kauai/Casper. 

*_Relief grants for farmers and ranchers_*

Farmers and ranchers whose agricultural lands were affected by Hurricane Lowell and other recent storms may apply for up to $1,500 through the state’s Emergency Farmer Relief grant program. Applications close Jan. 29, 2027.


  * Farms, orchards, ranches, and similar operations statewide are eligible. Limit one $1,500 check per applicant per year. 
  * Applicants must provide tax documents such as a W-9, Schedule C, or Schedule F. 
  * Funding is limited. If applications exceed available funds, they will be processed first-come, first-served. 
  * Checks are expected to be available for pickup statewide starting early to mid-January. Applicants will be notified of the time and place. 

  * Apply at https://dab.hawaii.gov. For questions, email dab.info@hawaii.gov or call (808) 973-9560. 

*_Business Recovery Grants_*

Due to high demand, the Kauaʻi Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program is no longer accepting applications. Businesses and nonprofits can join the waitlist at https://kauaibusinessrecovery.org in case more funding becomes available.

*_Help for nonprofits_*

The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) is offering low-interest disaster loans of up to $2 million to eligible private nonprofit and faith-based organizations affected by Hurricane Lowell.


  * Deadlines are Dec. 7 for physical damage and July 7, 2027, for economic injury. 
  * Apply at https://www.sba.gov/disaster or call (866) 722-4357. 

*_Utilities_*


  * KIUC has restored power to most of the island. Members who need a payment plan or financial help can visit https://kiuc.coop/payment-assistance or call (808) 246-4300. 
  * The Department of Water’s Water Conservation Notice continues for customers in ʻAnini. Report outages or leaks at (808) 245-5444. 

*_Refuse and recycling_*


  * Seven debris and refuse sites are open islandwide, with tipping fees waived for storm debris. Hours and accepted materials are at https://www.kauairecovers.org/debris. 
  * North Shore refuse collection is on Thursdays only. 
  * Kauaʻi Recycles bins have permanently moved from the Hanalei Refuse Transfer Station to the Kīlauea Community Agricultural Center (ʻĀina Hoʻokupu o Kīlauea), 4045 Kīlauea Road. Hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Saturday. Closed Sundays and County holidays.

bullets: The Kapaʻa DMV is open by appointment only. Book at www.kauai.gov/DMV.

Walk-ins and kūpuna hour are not available.
Please bring cash or a check if possible, as card stations are limited.
Renew vehicle registration online at https://mvr.ehawaii.gov/renewals/kauai/lookup or at kiosks at Western Motors in Hanapēpē, Līhuʻe Safeway, Kapaʻa Safeway, and Princeville Foodland.
Request a duplicate driver’s license at https://mydmv.hnl.info/hnldl/duplicates.
A temporary DMV location is being prepared at the Gather space in Līhuʻe. An opening date has not been set.
For questions, call (808) 241-1949 or email kauaidmv@kauai.gov.

paragraphs: The County is covering the $2.50 convenience fee for online vehicle registration renewals and sewer payments.

Hanapēpē Stadium
Morgan's Pond at Lydgate Beach Park is closed until further notice due to logs and fine wood particles in and around the area.
The Kekaha Neighborhood Center is accepting new online reservations at www.kauai.gov/parks.

REMINDER: EISPN Notice and Waiahi Surface Water Treatment Plant public scoping meeting Nov. 10 & 12

LĪHUʻE - The Kaua‘i Department of Water (KDOW) is publishing the Environmental Impact Statement Preparation Notice (EISPN) for the acquisition and expansion of the Waiahi Surface Water Treatment Plant and Upgrade of the Related Waterline Transmission System (“Project”) for public review. The *EISPN document will be available to download* from the* State of Hawaii - Environmental Review Program website on November 8, 2026:*

Website: https://planning.hawaii.gov/erp/environmental-notice/ 

Direct link to EISPN (accessible on November 8): https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/erp/Doc_Library/2026-11-08-KA-EISPN-Waiahi-Surface-Water-Treatment-Plant-and-Transmission-System.pdf 

The EISPN publication and public review period provides an opportunity for agencies and the public to provide input on the environmental, social, and technical issues that should be evaluated as part of the draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) being prepared. The 30-day public review period is from November 8 to December 8, 2026. *The deadline for submitting comments is December 8, 2026. *

KDOW invites the public to attend the EISPN scoping meetings to learn more about the Project and share their feedback. Two EISPN scoping meetings will be held during the 30-day public review period: *              *

*EISPN Scoping Meeting (Virtual) *

*Date/Time:* November 10, 2026, at 5 p.m.
*Access Link: *    https://us06web.zoom.us/j/81073415164

To learn more about the Project or to submit general or EISPN comments, visit https://waiahi-swtp-eis.com/ .

items.body:
*Nov. 6, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

LĪHUʻE – Please see the latest updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services below.

*Hurricane Lowell Recovery*

*Emergency food distribution*

The County of Kauaʻi is partnering with Hawaiʻi Foodbank Kauaʻi to hold an emergency food distribution today for residents affected by Hurricane Lowell. This is a mobile pantry distribution. Please bring reusable bags or totes.

*Today, Friday, Nov. 6*

Hale Līhuʻe, 4286 Rice St., Līhuʻe, 4 to 5 p.m. Turn into the parking lot from the Convention Hall, then exit toward Rice Street (right turn only).

To respect local traffic, please line up no earlier than 15 minutes before the start time.

*Relief grants for farmers and ranchers*

Farmers and ranchers whose agricultural lands were affected by Hurricane Lowell and the other recent storms can apply for up to $1,500 through the state's Emergency Farmer Relief grant program. Applications will be accepted through Jan. 29, 2027.


  * Farms, orchards, ranches, and similar operations statewide are eligible. Each applicant can receive one $1,500 check per year. 
  * Applicants will need to submit tax documents, such as a W-9, Schedule C, or Schedule F, as proof of farming or ranching work. 
  * Funding is limited. If more eligible applications come in than funds allow, they will be processed first-come, first-served. 
  * Checks are expected to be available for pickup at locations statewide starting early to mid-January. Applicants will be told when and where to collect them. 
  * The application portal is at https://dab.hawaii.gov.  
  * Questions: dab.info@hawaii.gov or (808) 973-9560. 

*Hurricane Lowell CASPER survey*

The Hawaiʻi Department of Health's Kauaʻi District Health Office and the County of Kauaʻi will conduct a Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response (CASPER) survey Nov. 16 to 20 to learn about Hurricane Lowell impacts and ongoing recovery needs. The results will help guide local recovery work by county, state, and federal partners and community organizations.


  * Survey teams will go door to door in 30 randomly selected areas around the island. Seven homes in each area will be selected. 
  * Teams include Department of Health staff, supported by the Kauaʻi Medical Reserve Corps and KEMA. Team members will wear vests identifying them as part of the DOH survey team and will carry ID cards. 
  * The survey takes less than 10 minutes and is voluntary. Responses are confidential, and no names or addresses are collected. Households can choose to complete it by phone instead. 
  * Questions cover emergency supplies right after the storm, physical and economic impacts, health and well-being, and recovery needs. 
  * Results will be shared in a public report. Past Kauaʻi CASPER survey reports are at https://health.hawaii.gov/kauai/Casper. 

*Business Recovery Grants*

Due to high demand, the Kauaʻi Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program is no longer accepting applications. Businesses and nonprofits can join the waitlist at https://kauaibusinessrecovery.org in case more funding becomes available.

*Help for nonprofits*


  * *FEMA Public Assistance:* Private nonprofits that provide critical or essential services, including houses of worship, community centers, schools, and care facilities, may be reimbursed for storm cleanup and repairs. The deadline to submit a Request for Public Assistance is today, Friday, Nov. 6. The form takes a few minutes and does not commit an organization to anything. For help, email dod.hiema.publicassistance@hawaii.gov or visit https://www.fema.gov/assistance/public/apply. 
  * *SBA disaster loans:* Low-interest loans of up to $2 million are available to private nonprofit and faith-based organizations. Deadlines are Dec. 7 for physical damage and July 7, 2027, for economic injury. Apply at https://www.sba.gov/disaster or call (866) 722-4357.

sections.heading: Nov. 6, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update
paragraphs: LĪHUʻE – Please see the latest updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services below.

sections.heading: Emergency food distribution
paragraphs: The County of Kauaʻi is partnering with Hawaiʻi Foodbank Kauaʻi to hold an emergency food distribution today for residents affected by Hurricane Lowell. This is a mobile pantry distribution. Please bring reusable bags or totes.

sections.heading: Today, Friday, Nov. 6
paragraphs: Hale Līhuʻe, 4286 Rice St., Līhuʻe, 4 to 5 p.m. Turn into the parking lot from the Convention Hall, then exit toward Rice Street (right turn only).
To respect local traffic, please line up no earlier than 15 minutes before the start time.

bullets: Farms, orchards, ranches, and similar operations statewide are eligible. Each applicant can receive one $1,500 check per year.

Funding is limited. If more eligible applications come in than funds allow, they will be processed first-come, first-served.

sections.heading: Utilities (NEW)
paragraphs: KIUC has restored power to most of the island.
Members needing a payment plan or financial help can visit https://kiuc.coop/payment-assistance or call (808) 246-4300.
The Department of Water continues its Water Conservation Notice for customers in ʻAnini. Report outages or leaks at (808) 245-5444.

sections.heading: Refuse and recycling
bullets: Seven debris and refuse sites are open islandwide, and tipping fees are waived for storm debris. Hours and accepted materials are at https://www.kauairecovers.org/debris.
North Shore refuse collection is on Thursdays only.

Kauaʻi Recycles bins have permanently moved from the Hanalei Refuse Transfer Station to the Kīlauea Community Agricultural Center (ʻĀina Hoʻokupu o Kīlauea), 4045 Kīlauea Road. Hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Saturday, closed Sundays and County holidays. The mobile recycling unit still visits Anaina Hou Community Park in Kīlauea on Tuesdays and Fridays, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

sections.heading: Storm repairs and property tax relief
bullets: If your home or building was built with a County permit and is not in a flood zone, you do not need a new permit to repair Hurricane Lowell damage. Work must still meet building codes.

Properties in a flood zone or near the shoreline need County review before work begins. Flood zone: call Public Works at (808) 241-4883. Shoreline: email planningdepartment@kauai.gov. Other questions: call the Building Division at (808) 241-4854.
Owners of storm-damaged property have until June 30, 2027, to file for disaster tax relief at https://www.kauai.gov/Residents/Report-Hurricane-Lowell-Property-Damage.
paragraphs: County of Kauaʻi Services*

sections.heading: Division of Motor Vehicles
bullets: The Kapaʻa DMV is open by appointment only. Book at www.kauai.gov/DMV. Space is limited, and early appointments are expected to go to people whose licenses, state IDs, or other credentials expired during the closure.
Walk-ins and kūpuna hour are not available. Bring cash or a check if you can, since card stations are limited.

Renew vehicle registration online at https://mvr.ehawaii.gov/renewals/kauai/lookup or at kiosks at Western Motors in Hanapēpē, Līhuʻe Safeway, Kapaʻa Safeway, and Princeville Foodland. Request a duplicate driver's license at https://mydmv.hnl.info/hnldl/duplicates.
A temporary DMV location is being prepared at the Gather space in Līhuʻe. An opening date has not been set.
Questions: (808) 241-1949 or kauaidmv@kauai.gov.

sections.heading: Online payments
paragraphs: The County is covering the $2.50 convenience fee for online vehicle registration renewals and sewer payments.

sections.heading: Parks, facilities, and transit
bullets: Closed: Waimea Neighborhood Center main hall (side rooms open), Waimea pools, Wailua Golf Course driving range, Salt Pond Beach Park and pavilions, and Hanapēpē Stadium.
The Poʻipū Beach Park parking lot is closed through today, Nov. 6, for maintenance and storm repairs.
Morgans Pond at Lydgate Beach Park is closed until further notice due to the presence of logs and fine wood particles in and surrounding the area.
The Kekaha Neighborhood Center is accepting new reservations online. Visit www.kauai.gov/parks.
The Kauaʻi Bus 900 and 950 express routes are not running.

sections.heading: County of Kauaʻi alerts
paragraphs: To sign up for Everbridge, the County's emergency notification service, visit https://www.kauai.gov/KEMA and click “Notification Services,” text “KAUAIEMA” to 888777, or call KEMA at (808) 241-1800.
Updates, working County phone numbers, and visitor information are at https://www.kauairecovers.org.
